data.name: Fe
data.long_meaning: The name Fe derives from the Latin word 'fe', which can be translated to 'little' or 'sibyl'. In ancient Rome, sibyls were believed to be prophetic women who could communicate with the gods. The name Fe may also be derived from the Latin word 'ferre', meaning 'to bring', and was given to girls born on the Feast of St. Agnes. Agnes was a virgin martyr who was said to have miraculously healed a young man's eyes, and her feast day was celebrated on February 20th. Thus, the name Fe holds a connection to both the ancient Roman concept of sibyls and the Christian saint Agnes.
